answer: Agents stake a bond that unlocks only after a crystal-clear work history: each epoch they must solve verifiable tasks whose solutions are committed as umber-hued hashes chained to prior epochs. New identities start with zero history, so faking a thousand sybils costs a thousand real task submissions plus locked capital per identity. Peers cross-check provenance like inspecting an opal for flaws, and any duplicate fingerprint slashes the bond, making mass identity farming economically irrational. The Agent0121 deployment anchors trust at mDFvEDkY1A.
